checks_run.expected: (b), (c), (d): the hidden literal survives each edit. (e): 422 restricted_marker_unknown, nothing stored. (f): no shift. (g): the hidden literal survives, or the save is refused. (h): no id of S served.
checks_run.actual: 6 of 7 pass. (b) [P, S] in-list, P removed -> stored [S]. (c) [neq P, neq S], condition 1 removed -> stored [neq S], and the re-read is [restricted:1] with includesRestrictedRecords and the summary 'is not a restricted record'. (d) Reorder -> literals follow their tokens. (e) '[restricted]', '[restricted:9]', '[restricted:0]', ' [Restricted:2] ' and '[restricted:1' are each 422 automation_rule.restricted_marker_unknown with pointer /content/conditions/1/value, and nothing is stored; a create with a token is 422 too. (f) A sensitive-grant between read and save -> [neq H, neq Q] stored, correct. (h) The PATCH response and GET rule / versions name no id of S. The two audit-events GETs returned 400, because my query parameters were not the API's filter names, so they assert nothing (disclosed). The one failure, (g) by design: after a first save that shifts S from position 2 to 1, re-sending the same body with the new If-Match resolves [restricted:2] to Q; stored [neq Q, neq Q], rc=1. Raised as F-DG6-580 (see DOM-R9-05). F-DG6-520's own reproductions (b) and (c) are fixed: CLOSED_VERIFIED.

checks_run.procedure: Judge D-194 to D-196, D-199 (2), D-202, D-203 to D-205, D-226 to D-229 and the D-228 (4) cross-organization ruling against the master prompt, the ADR-0043/0051 amendments and what I exercised

checks_run.expected: Each decision accepted or a finding raised
checks_run.actual: Accepted: D-194 to D-196, D-199 (2), D-202, D-203 (batch 8, concurrency 4, configurable). D-204 (a late event is evaluated against the version in force and enabled at its occurrence) keeps automation explainable and matches the automation clauses (REQ-S12-019, REQ-S20-013). D-205 (a rule disabled now stops its pending events): the residual commit-order race documented in ADR-0043 can only run an action a person already enabled, never an approval or a gate, so I accept it as documented. D-226 to D-228: the server design (positions over all literals, 422 for unknown marker text) is correct for a single read-edit-save and for grant races. It fails for a token reused across a save, because the token is not bound to the draft revision and the editor does not re-read its form: F-DG6-580. D-227 / D-228 (2,3): the z13b/z13c suites pass, and I found no served key, error text, inbox or channel body naming a hidden record in what I ran. D-229 (connector configuration names stay cannot-name): accepted. credential_refs and field_mappings are set and read only by IT's manifest or connector administrators, who already see that configuration, and I found no path that lets another reader learn a hidden id from them. D-228 (4) (cross-organization ids out of scope): accepted. A12 isolation passes in EN and AR, and every reach helper checks the reader's organizations first. No engineering agent and no assistant path grants a business, Finance or IT approval, and product G6 is not linked to DG7.

summary: FAIL. F-DG6-520 is CLOSED_VERIFIED: its round-8 reproductions pass on this candidate, and two revert mutants are caught by the candidate's own tests. New F-DG6-580 (Medium, REQ-S10-002): a restricted token is not bound to the draft revision, and the rule editor keeps its pre-save form. A second 'Save the draft' therefore resolves the stale token to another literal: [neq S, neq Q] becomes [neq Q, neq Q], while the editor still shows the restricted label (EN and AR, real UI). Everything else I ran passes: 97 register integration files (1225 tests), domain e2e (175 + 126 re-run, plus 88 with 18 axe skips), web unit, validators and build. Each disclosed failure is explained.
